task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's Step 4 suite for ISS-0442: independently reproduce the mutation-kill (not trust the reported counts), independently verify Jason's duplicate-key semantics and judge whether the newly-found gap must block this gate, re-verify every other coverage claim by reading the test code directly, and re-verify the flagged flaky-test class.

result.summary:
MUTATION-KILL RE-VERIFICATION (performed myself, not copied from TEST-DESIGNER's or REVIEWER's reported numbers): created a throwaway `git worktree add /tmp/claude-1001/wt-iss0442-validate HEAD`, symlinked deps/_build from the main tree (no network access needed), applied the exact mutant (`if depth == 1 and key_follows?(after_string) do` -> `if key_follows?(after_string) do` in handle_string_token/5), and ran `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs`. Measured myself: 'Finished in 9.5 seconds' / 'Result: 45/47 passed' / 'Failed: 2 tests' -- the two failures were exactly `T-SPLICE-PRESERVES-ESCAPES-BRACES-ARRAY-NO-NEWLINE` and `T-AUTOFIX-NESTED-STATUS-COLLISION-PASS-PASS`, both raising `Mix.Error: letflow.lint_handoffs found 1 new violation(s)` -- i.e. under the mutant the top-level status is left unfixed (the nested, higher-depth `result.status` candidate wins instead), exactly the corruption mechanism named in REVIEWER's Step 3 handoff and in test/specs/ISS-0442.md. Cleaned up via `git worktree remove /tmp/claude-1001/wt-iss0442-validate --force`; confirmed no mutant was ever applied to the tracked main worktree: `git status --porcelain` in the main repo returned empty throughout (the mutation only ever touched the throwaway worktree's own copy of the file). Re-ran the real, unmutated code afterward in the main tree: `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 9.3 seconds' / 'Result: 47 passed', zero failures. This satisfies the mandatory mutant-isolation-and-revert-and-verify procedure for a 'code under test does not exist' pre-fix case -- REVIEWER's REQUIRED acceptance criterion (T-AUTOFIX-NESTED-STATUS-COLLISION-PASS-PASS) is confirmed load-bearing by my own measurement, not by reading TEST-DESIGNER's claim.

DUPLICATE-TOP-LEVEL-STATUS-KEY GAP -- INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AND JUDGED NOT BLOCKING: reproduced the Jason claim myself via `MIX_ENV=test LETFLOW_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32) mix run --no-start -e 'IO.inspect(Jason.decode!(~s({\"status\":\"a\",\"status\":\"b\"})))'` -> `%{\"status\" => \"a\"}`, confirming Jason on this pinned version is FIRST-key-wins, contradicting the design doc's §2.2 step 2 'mirrors Jason.decode/1's own last-key-wins semantics' claim, while `scan_for_status/4`'s `best` accumulator is genuinely last-MATCH-wins. This is a real logic discrepancy: for a duplicate-top-level-status-key document, `--autofix` would splice a different span than the one `autofix_file/1` decided to fix based on, producing a file that fails its own next lint pass. However, judged NOT exploitable in practice and NOT a blocker for this gate: (1) I independently wrote a Python script using `object_pairs_hook` to detect duplicate keys in the ROOT object of every real handoff file in the corpus (not a naive grep on 'status' occurrences, which would false-positive on every file with both a top-level and nested result.status) -- scanned all 1989 `handoffs/**/step*.json` files, found ZERO files with any duplicate top-level key, let alone a duplicate 'status' key; (2) a duplicate top-level key is itself malformed/non-canonical JSON that no producing agent's own JSON-encoding pathway in this codebase has ever emitted (Jason.encode! cannot produce a duplicate key from a decoded map, so the only way one could appear is hand-edited or externally-corrupted input, outside this tool's normal operating envelope); (3) the failure mode is self-limiting, not silently-wrong-forever -- the very next lint pass immediately re-flags a fresh H1 violation on the file, so a corrupted fix is loudly visible on the next CI run rather than silently accepted. TEST-DESIGNER's documentation in test/specs/ISS-0442.md's 'Known gap' section, plus the code comment block at test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:722-741, correctly state the mechanism, correctly avoid asserting the buggy behavior as correct, and correctly flag it as a follow-up rather than working around it with a misleading test. Judgment: appropriate to leave as a follow-up issue rather than block this gate. Per this run's own instructions, I am NOT filing that issue myself -- flagging it explicitly below for ORCH to route via the queue after this run completes.

OTHER COVERAGE RE-VERIFICATION (read the actual test code directly, not the summary): T-AUTOFIX-NESTED-STATUS-COLLISION-PASS-PASS (test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:756-814) asserts decoded top-level status == COMPLETED, decoded nested result.status == PASS (unchanged), AND full-file byte-identity against a hand-built `expected` string -- the strongest check. T-SPLICE-PRESERVES-ESCAPES-BRACES-ARRAY-NO-NEWLINE (816-843) uses a fixture with an escaped quote, a literal unbalanced brace inside a string value, and an inline array, all nested inside 'context' (deliberately avoiding tripping the unrelated H3 non-schema-key check, per the file's own comment) -- asserts full-file byte-identity plus explicit no-trailing-newline. T-AUTOFIX-REFUSES-MISSING-STATUS (845-859) and T-AUTOFIX-REFUSES-NULL-STATUS (861-875) both drive the real `run/1 --autofix` / `--dir` path via `LintHandoffs.run([\"--dir\", dir, \"--autofix\"])` (not a direct `lint_file/2` call), assert byte-identity and the REFUSED report text -- correctly closing the gap the design's §3 'preserved behavior' names, previously only exercised via direct `lint_file/2` calls that never touch the autofix/refusal machinery. All four tests are new, non-redundant with the 43 pre-existing tests (grep-confirmed: T-AUTOFIX-DOES-NOT-TOUCH-NESTED-RESULT-STATUS at line 652 uses an already-legal top-level COMPLETED, hitting :skip before ever reaching the splice code -- distinct from the new PASS/PASS collision fixture that reaches the splice branch). No `@tag :skip`, `@tag :pending`, or 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in the file (grep, zero matches). Each test's `setup` block creates its own fresh tmp dir via `System.tmp_dir!() |> Path.join(\"letflow-iss0442-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}\")` with `on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf!(dir) end)` -- self-sufficient, no shared hardcoded fixture state, no ordering dependency between tests. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in any new test.

FLAKY-TEST CLAIM -- RE-VERIFIED MYSELF: re-ran `mix test test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs test/letflow/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs` in isolation -> 'Finished in 11.3 seconds' / 'Result: 12 passed', zero failures, matching TEST-DESIGNER's own reported isolation-run result exactly. Confirmed via `git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0442-20260904 --stat -- test/ lib/` that this branch's entire diff touches only 4 files: the design doc, `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex`, `test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs`, and the new `test/specs/ISS-0442.md` -- nothing under `test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs` or `test/letflow/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs`, and no shared module either touches tenant schema provisioning/reaping or identity migration. Judgment confirmed: this is the known shared-Postgres async-suite flake class (schema/connection races under full concurrent test load), not an interaction with this branch's changes.

Verdict: PASS. All acceptance criteria have runnable, non-redundant, self-sufficient coverage; REVIEWER's REQUIRED mutation-killing criterion is independently confirmed load-bearing by my own measurement; the newly-found duplicate-key gap is real but correctly scoped out and documented rather than blocking; the flaky-test claim is independently confirmed as the known unrelated flake class.

issues.description: Duplicate-top-level-status-key defect (pre-existing in ELIXIR-DEV's Step 2 implementation, first found by TEST-DESIGNER, independently re-verified by this validator): for a document with a duplicate top-level 'status' key, autofix_file/1's Jason-decode-based read (first-key-wins on this pinned Jason version) disagrees with splice_top_level_status/2's raw-text scan (last-match-wins per the design's own, factually incorrect, 'mirrors Jason.decode/1's last-key-wins' claim in §2.2 step 2) about which occurrence is 'the' status, so --autofix edits the wrong span and the file re-fails its own very next lint pass. Verified zero occurrences of ANY duplicate top-level key in the real handoffs/ corpus (1989 files scanned via a Python json.loads object_pairs_hook check, not a naive grep) -- not currently exploitable, and self-limiting (loudly re-flagged on the next lint pass, not silently wrong forever). NOT a blocker for this gate. Recommend ORCH file a new issue (ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis + a design/code correction, likely fixing either the design's semantic claim or making the scan's tie-break rule match Jason's actual first-key-wins behavior) via the queue after this run completes -- do not treat TEST-DESIGNER's or this validator's documentation of it as sufficient resolution on its own.
